def transform(grid):
    # The grid is a tiled rectangular array: thick separator rows/columns mark cells.
    # Each intersection of a pair of divider lines carries the encoded marker color.
    # Extract marker patterns at divider intersections, preserving their arrangement.
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # identify full-ish lines with distinct divider value (not background or fill)
    # In demonstrations separators are color 8 and base fill 6; output records separator marker 2.
    div = next((v for v in set(sum(grid, [])) if all(v in row for row in grid)), None)
    if div is None:
        # find recurring uniform rows/cols
        divrows=[i for i,row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row))==1]
        divcols=[j for j in range(cols) if len({grid[i][j] for i in range(rows)})==1]
    else:
        divrows=[i for i,row in enumerate(grid) if all(x==div for x in row)]
        divcols=[j for j in range(cols) if all(grid[i][j]==div for i in range(rows))]
    # Intersections contain colored dots; output bitmap of marker counts per tile.
    # Select the non-divider color(s) on separator lines and map presence to that color.
    marks={x for row in grid for x in row if x not in (div,)}
    marks.discard(5); marks.discard(6)
    color=next(iter(marks), 2)
    rmarks=[]
    for r in divrows:
        vals=[]
        for c in divcols:
            vals.append(1 if grid[r][c]==color else 0)
        if any(vals): rmarks.append(vals)
    if not rmarks: return [[color]]
    activecols=[j for j in range(len(divcols)) if any(row[j] for row in rmarks)]
    active=[ [row[j] for j in activecols] for row in rmarks]
    # encode marked locations as marker color, unmarked as interior fill
    return [[color if v else next((x for x in sum(grid,[]) if x not in (div,color)),0) for v in row] for row in active]
